title: Arithmetic definability: enumerable sets and quantifiers
summary: An enumerable set is exactly a set described in arithmetic by an unbounded search followed by a bounded check.
abstract: A program can recognize a successful computation by checking a finite record. Arithmetic can describe the same record using numbers, addition and multiplication. We make this connection precise: a set is computably enumerable exactly when membership can be expressed by existentially choosing numbers and then checking a bounded arithmetic condition. Negating such a description gives a universal one, and having both kinds of description is exactly what permits a decision procedure. The halting set shows why a short arithmetic formula need not decide membership. We finish by reading a formula for total programs, where each input may need its own computation witness.
